title: Black spots on a radish: when you can trim them and when to toss it

seo.title: Black spots on radishes: trim or throw away?
seo.meta_description: A small dry superficial black mark may be trimmed if sound white flesh is immediately underneath. Deep, wet, soft, spreading spots or off odors mean discard the radish.
seo.search_intent: Distinguish superficial black marks on radishes from disease or decay that extends into the root.

excerpt: A small black spot that is dry and superficial can sometimes be trimmed away if the radish is firm and the flesh directly underneath is clean. If the lesion is sunken, wet, soft, spreading inward, moldy, or foul-smelling, discard the radish.
content_html:
A black mark stands out sharply against a red or white radish, but depth and texture tell you more than the color itself. Some marks are superficial damage; others are associated with disease or decay.

University of Minnesota Extension describes several root problems that can produce dark or sunken lesions, while UC Davis lists black spot and soft rots among radish postharvest disorders.

When a spot may be only skin-deep

If the mark is small, dry, and the radish remains hard, cut through it. If clean, firm flesh appears immediately underneath and there is no abnormal smell, trim the damaged area generously and use the rest promptly.

A dry scar or abrasion behaves differently from a lesion that has changed the texture of the root.

When to stop trimming

A black area that extends toward the center, feels sunken or wet, or is surrounded by soft tissue can represent disease or rot. If each new slice still shows dark, deteriorated flesh, discard the radish rather than carving it down piece by piece.

Look at the whole root

  • One dry scar, root firm: trim and inspect.
  • Several sunken or cracked lesions: poor quality; inspect closely.
  • Dark tissue extending into soft flesh: discard.
  • Slime, mold, or unpleasant odor: discard.

A pithy old radish can also have a dry spongy center, but that is different from a wet black lesion. When both are present, judge the radish by the more serious sign.

Dry and superficial may be trimmable; dark, wet, and deep is a reason to toss the root. A cross-section tells you whether the problem ended at the skin or continued inward.

faq.question: Can I cut a black spot off a radish?
faq.answer: Yes, if the spot is small, dry, superficial, and clean firm flesh appears immediately underneath.

faq.question: Are black spots on radishes always mold?
faq.answer: No. They can come from injury or plant diseases as well as decay; wetness, softness, depth, and spreading damage matter more than color alone.

faq.question: When should I throw the whole radish away?
faq.answer: Discard it when dark damage extends into the flesh or appears with soft rot, slime, mold, or an off odor.
